paper.title: Efficient Poverty Mapping from High Resolution Remote Sensing Images
paper.authors: Ayush, Uzkent, Tanmay, Burke, Lobell, Ermon

detector_report.weights: yolov3u.pt (COCO) fine-tuned on xView parent classes

detector_caveat: YOLOv3 initialised from COCO weights and fine-tuned on xView parent classes, as the paper specifies. Features are genuine overhead object counts.

gsd_leakage.note: Native HR GSD is retained (no global resampling). Because every subtile covers the same 70 m footprint and is resized to a common 224 px before detection, the effective inference GSD is 0.311 m/px for every cluster -- so scrape zoom does NOT change apparent object size. What it does change is sharpness: a coarse cluster is upsampled and blurry. This correlation bounds how much of the downstream signal could ride on that sharpness difference rather than on image content.
